name: Slovakia
summary: Slovakia exempts gains on listed shares held over one year (foreign exchanges included), taxes dividends at 7%, and has no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. The catch is a private business sale or short-term trading, which is taxed at up to 35% from 2026 plus 15% uncapped health insurance (about 50% at the top).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Progressive PIT (19/25/30/35% from 2026) with exemptions for long-held listed securities and real estate; 7% dividends.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident with permanent residence, a habitual home with intent to stay, or 183+ days in a calendar year.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on securities admitted to trading on an EU regulated market or a comparable foreign regulated market are exempt if held more than one year (§9(1)(k) ZDP). Other gains (unlisted shares, stakes in a limited company, listed shares sold within a year) are 'other income' under §8, which §4(1)(a) puts in the general tax base taxed at the progressive 19%/25%/30%/35% rates (§15(a)(1)); the separate 19% base is only for §7 capital income such as interest. Taxable §8 income also bears 15% public health insurance on the same base with no cap. Real estate held more than 5 years is exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Listed securities held > 1 year (and listed > 1 year): exempt (§9(1)(k) ZDP). Real estate held > 5 years: exempt (§9(1)(a)). EUR 500 a year exemption for net other income including securities gains (§9(1)(i)). Gains inside the long-term investment savings scheme (DIS) exempt after 15 years.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Not for securities held as business assets or received as employee benefits in kind.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: No holding-period exemption for unlisted shares or s.r.o. stakes: a private business sale is taxed at up to 35% plus 15% health insurance, about 50% at the top for a person insured in the Slovak public system. Health insurance: §10b(1)(d) and §13(7) of Act 580/2004 make the §8 tax base an assessment base, rate 15% (§12(1)(b)); the only cap in §13 is the 60x average-wage cap for dividends (§13(6)). A resident covered by another EU state's social security under Regulation 883/2004 would not pay it. 2026 brackets: 25% above 154.8x, 30% above 212.4x, 35% above 264x the subsistence minimum.

open_questions: PwC describes capital gains as falling in a separate 19% base; the law (§8(1)(e)-(f), §4(1)(a), §15(a)(1)-(4) ZDP, version effective 1 Jan 2026) puts gains on securities and company stakes in the general progressive base and reserves the separate 19% base for §7 capital income. We follow the law text.
Euro amounts of the 2026 bracket thresholds (multiples of the subsistence minimum valid on 1 Jan 2026) not computed here.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Listed securities held > 1 year: exempt (foreign regulated markets included). Private company stake: top marginal PIT 35% (2026) plus 15% health insurance on the same taxable gain = 0.50 for a Slovak-insured resident. Real estate held > 5 years: exempt. headline_rate 0.35 is the top statutory PIT rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities held as business assets are excluded from the exemption and taxed as business income.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 1 year for listed securities; 5 years for real estate; none for unlisted shares.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents taxed on worldwide income; the exemption explicitly covers comparable foreign regulated markets.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid out of profits for 2025 onwards are taxed at 7% (10% applied to 2024 profits), withheld at source by Slovak companies and self-assessed in a separate base for foreign dividends. Dividends from non-cooperative jurisdictions: 35%. No health insurance on dividends from 2017+ profits.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Dividends from 2004-2016 profits are not taxed.

sources.title: Slovak Republic - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: The foreign tax credit is read in the law text (§45(1) ZDP, 2026-10-16): where a treaty uses the credit method, the foreign tax is credited up to the rate the treaty allows the source state to levy and up to the Slovak tax on that income. With a 15% foreign withholding and a 7% Slovak tax, the Slovak tax on the foreign dividend is therefore 0.
dividends.rate_basis: §15(a)(5) ZDP: 7% on the separate dividend base (§51e(3)(a)); 35% for dividends from non-cooperative states (§15(a)(6)). Foreign WHT credited under treaties, so typical 15% WHT leaves no Slovak tax. Foreign dividends of resident individuals go into the separate base of §51e(1)(a), (3)(a) ZDP at 7% (§15(a)(5)); the credit is §45(1) ZDP.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 7% WHT on dividends to individuals; 35% to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions or with unidentified beneficial owners.
dividends.treaty_network: Broad network covering the EU, the US and most OECD states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Slovak CIT is 10%/21%/24% by taxable income; distribution to an individual then bears 7%. A Slovak holding s.r.o. was considered (2026-10-16): the company would pay 21% on gains from portfolio shares (not read in the statute; PwC) while an individual holding listed shares for more than a year pays nothing, and a payout to the individual bears 7% again, so it is not better than holding personally. Slovakia has no private foundation or family trust for private wealth (a nadácia is a public-benefit vehicle).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local real estate tax set by municipalities; not a wealth tax.

inheritance.summary: There is no inheritance or gift tax, and income acquired by gift or inheritance is outside the scope of income tax for every recipient.

open_questions: Notary probate fees not quantified; treated as negligible.
inheritance.gift_tax: None; gifts and inheritances are not subject to income tax (§12(7)(b) ZDP: income acquired by gift or inheritance is not an object of the tax).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has permanent residence in Slovakia, a home there not only for occasional use with evident intent to stay permanently, or is present 183+ days in a calendar year (study and medical stays excluded); treaty tie-breakers apply.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit
routes.requirements: Purpose-based permit (business, employment, family); no investor programme found (unverified).

corporate.summary: From 2025: 10% for taxable revenue up to EUR 100,000, 21% standard, 24% for revenue above EUR 5 million (§15(b) ZDP, 2026 version). Minimum tax rules apply.
